title.value: A Comparative Analysis of Expected and Distributional Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title is taken directly from the document header and is consistent with the abstract and introduction content.
title.quote: Title: A Comparative Analysis of Expected and Distributional Reinforcement Learning

analysis.description: The paper investigates the differences between distributional and expected reinforcement learning methods. It examines these differences in various settings including tabular, linear approximation, and non-linear approximation. The paper provides both theoretical proofs and empirical evaluations to identify cases where distributional reinforcement learning behaves the same as or differently from expected reinforcement learning.

type.justification: The paper provides empirical analysis alongside theoretical evaluations to understand the performance differences between distributional and expected reinforcement learning methods.
type.quote: We then continue with an empirical analysis comparing dis- tributional and expected RL methods in control settings with non-linear approximators to tease apart where the improve- ments from distributional RL methods are coming from.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on reinforcement learning, comparing different reinforcement learning approaches.
name.quote: In this paper we begin the investigation into this fundamental question by analyzing the differences in the tabular, linear approximation, and non-linear approx- imation settings.

name.justification: The paper specifically deals with distributional approaches to reinforcement learning, discussing algorithms like C51 and their benefits over traditional methods.
name.quote: Since their introduction a year ago, distributional approaches to reinforcement learning (distributional RL) have produced strong results relative to the standard approach which models expected values (expected RL).

name.justification: C51 is mentioned as the first distributional reinforcement learning algorithm, showing dramatic improvements in performance, particularly in Atari games.
name.quote: The first distributional reinforcement learning algorithm, C51, saw dramatic improvements in performance in many Atari 2600 games when compared to an algorithm that only modelled expected values (Bellemare, Dabney, and Munos 2017).

is_contributed.justification: The paper discusses C51 as an existing model, not as a contribution by the authors of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: ...distributional reinforcement learning algorithm, C51, saw dramatic improvements...

is_executed.justification: The paper does not explicitly state that C51 is executed as part of this study, it is rather used as a reference model.

is_compared.justification: The performance of C51 and other distributional methods is compared against expected value methods in the paper.
is_compared.quote: We prove that in many realizations of the tabular and linear approximation settings, distributional RL behaves exactly the same as expected RL...
